title: JetStream stream configuration
markdownDescription:
A JetStream **StreamConfig** — the same JSON as `nats stream add --config <file>` and `nats stream info --json | jq .config`.

File name: `<STREAM>.stream.json`. Use **Plan & Apply Config Folder** or the CodeLens above to compare with and apply to a connection.

Fields you omit keep their server value (or the server default when the stream is created). Durations are **nanoseconds**.

source.markdownDescription: A stream to replicate from (mirror or source).

name.markdownDescription: Name of the origin stream (in this account / domain, or remote with `external` / `domain`).

opt_start_seq.markdownDescription: Start replicating at this stream sequence of the origin.

opt_start_time.markdownDescription: Start replicating with messages stored at or after this time (RFC 3339, e.g. `2026-01-01T00:00:00Z`).

filter_subject.markdownDescription: Only replicate messages whose subject matches this filter (wildcards allowed). Use `subject_transforms` for several filters.

external.markdownDescription: Origin stream in another account or JetStream domain, reached through an imported API prefix. Mutually exclusive with `domain`.

api.markdownDescription: JetStream API prefix of the remote stream, e.g. `$JS.hub.API` for domain `hub`.

deliver.markdownDescription: Delivery subject prefix used for the replication consumer (when the remote account exports a deliver subject).

domain.markdownDescription: Convenience for `external`: the JetStream domain of the origin stream. The client converts it to `external.api = $JS.<domain>.API`; it is never sent to the server. Mutually exclusive with `external`.

items.markdownDescription: Subject mapping applied to messages as they are stored (server 2.10+). Uses the same mapping syntax as account subject mappings, e.g. `{{wildcard(1)}}`, `{{partition(3,1)}}`.

src.markdownDescription: Source subject filter the transform applies to (wildcards allowed). Empty = all subjects of the stream / source.

subject_transforms.markdownDescription: Subject transforms applied to replicated messages (server 2.10+). Each entry may also act as a filter (`src`).

consumer.markdownDescription: Use a pre-created durable consumer on the origin for sourcing / mirroring instead of an ephemeral ordered consumer (server 2.14+, ADR-60). The consumer must exist first and use `ack_policy: "flow_control"`.

name.markdownDescription: Name of the pre-created durable consumer on the origin stream.

deliver_subject.markdownDescription: Must equal the `deliver_subject` of that consumer.

subjectTransform.markdownDescription: Subject mapping applied to messages as they are stored (server 2.10+). Uses the same mapping syntax as account subject mappings, e.g. `{{wildcard(1)}}`, `{{partition(3,1)}}`.

src.markdownDescription: Source subject filter the transform applies to (wildcards allowed). Empty = all subjects of the stream / source.

$schema.markdownDescription: Optional JSON schema reference (ignored when applying).

name.markdownDescription:
Stream name. **Must match the file name** (`<name>.stream.json`). Cannot contain whitespace, `.`, `*`, `>`, `/` or `\`.

Renaming means creating a new stream.
name.errorMessage: Stream names cannot contain whitespace, '.', '*', '>', '/' or '\'

description.markdownDescription: Short human description of the stream's purpose.

subjects.markdownDescription:
Subjects the stream captures. Wildcards: `*` matches one token, `>` the rest (e.g. `orders.>`).

Must be empty for a mirror; may be empty when `sources` are set. Can be changed on an existing stream — removing a subject stops capturing it (stored messages stay). Plans compare subjects as a set (order is ignored).

markdownEnumDescriptions: Keep messages until a limit (`max_msgs`, `max_bytes`, `max_age`, per-subject limits) is reached, then apply the `discard` policy. **Default.**
Keep a message while at least one consumer has not yet acknowledged it; messages without interest are removed.
Each message is consumed once: removed as soon as one consumer acknowledges it. Consumers must not overlap.
retention.markdownDescription:
How messages are retained.

An existing stream can switch between `limits` and `interest`, but ⛔ **not to or from `workqueue`**.

max_consumers.markdownDescription: Maximum number of consumers this stream allows. `-1` = unlimited (`0` is treated as unlimited).

max_msgs.markdownDescription:
Maximum number of messages kept. `-1` = unlimited. When exceeded, the `discard` policy applies.

⚠ Lowering it on an existing stream deletes the oldest messages (discard `old`).

max_bytes.markdownDescription:
Maximum total size of the stream. `-1` = unlimited. Some accounts require a value (`max_bytes_required`).

⚠ Lowering it on an existing stream deletes the oldest messages (discard `old`).

**Unit: bytes.** `1048576` = 1 MiB · `1073741824` = 1 GiB.

max_age.markdownDescription:
Maximum age of a message. `0` = keep forever.

⚠ Lowering it on an existing stream deletes older messages immediately.

**Unit: nanoseconds** (JetStream API). `1000000000` = 1 s · `60000000000` = 1 min · `3600000000000` = 1 h · `86400000000000` = 24 h.

max_msgs_per_subject.markdownDescription: Messages kept **per subject** (useful for last-value semantics, like KV history). `-1` = unlimited.

max_msg_size.markdownDescription:
Largest message accepted (payload + headers). `-1` = unlimited (bounded by the server's `max_payload`).

**Unit: bytes.** `1048576` = 1 MiB · `1073741824` = 1 GiB.

markdownEnumDescriptions: Keep messages in memory only — lost when the server restarts (replicas excepted).
storage.markdownDescription:
Storage backend.

⛔ **Immutable** — cannot be changed on an existing stream; the plan flags the change and apply is blocked. Recreate the stream instead.

markdownEnumDescriptions: Delete the oldest messages to make room. **Default.**
Reject new publishes with an error (the publisher sees a failed PubAck).
discard.markdownDescription: What happens when a limit is reached.

discard_new_per_subject.markdownDescription: With `discard: "new"` and `max_msgs_per_subject`, reject new messages per subject instead of for the whole stream.

num_replicas.markdownDescription: Number of replicas (1, 3 or 5 in practice). Requires a clustered JetStream for values > 1. Can be changed on an existing stream (the cluster re-replicates).

no_ack.markdownDescription: Do not send a PubAck for messages stored by this stream (fire-and-forget publishing; only for core NATS publishers that don't wait for acks).

duplicate_window.markdownDescription:
Window for duplicate detection with the `Nats-Msg-Id` header. `0` = server default (2 minutes, or `max_age` when that is shorter).

Must not be larger than a non-zero `max_age`. When a file lowers `max_age` below the current window and does not set `duplicate_window`, Apply lowers the window to `max_age` (the server rejects the update otherwise).

**Unit: nanoseconds** (JetStream API). `1000000000` = 1 s · `60000000000` = 1 min · `3600000000000` = 1 h · `86400000000000` = 24 h.

placement.markdownDescription: Placement directives for the stream's replicas (clustered JetStream). Random placement when unset.

cluster.markdownDescription: Cluster to place the stream in.

tags.markdownDescription: Server tags the replicas must match (`server_tags` in the server config), e.g. `["az:eu-1"]`.

mirror.markdownDescription:
Make this stream a 1:1 **mirror** of another stream. A mirror has no `subjects` and no `sources`.

⛔ **Immutable** — cannot be changed on an existing stream; the plan flags the change and apply is blocked. Recreate the stream instead.

sources.markdownDescription: Streams whose messages are replicated into this stream (aggregation). Can be changed on an existing stream.

sealed.markdownDescription:
Seal the stream: no more messages, deletes or purges; limits stop applying.

The server only accepts this through an update — when Apply creates a stream with `sealed: true` it creates it first, then seals it.

⚠ **One-way** — can be turned on with an update but never turned off again.

deny_delete.markdownDescription:
Forbid deleting individual messages through the API.

⚠ **One-way** — can be turned on with an update but never turned off again.

deny_purge.markdownDescription:
Forbid purging the stream through the API.

⚠ **One-way** — can be turned on with an update but never turned off again.

allow_rollup_hdrs.markdownDescription: Allow the `Nats-Rollup` header to replace the stream's (or a subject's) contents with a single message. Requires purge permission.

allow_direct.markdownDescription: Allow direct get (`$JS.API.DIRECT.GET`): faster reads served by any replica, possibly slightly stale. KV buckets enable it by default.

mirror_direct.markdownDescription: For mirrors: also answer direct gets for the origin stream's subjects.

republish.markdownDescription: Republish every stored message to a core NATS subject (cheap fan-out, KV watchers).

src.markdownDescription: Subject filter of the messages to republish (wildcards allowed). Default: all.

headers_only.markdownDescription: Republish headers only (no payload); a `Nats-Msg-Size` header carries the payload size.

metadata.markdownDescription:
Free-form string metadata stored with the stream (server 2.10+), e.g. owner, team, ticket.

Keys starting with `_nats` are reserved: the server adds `_nats.ver`, `_nats.level` … itself and plans ignore them.

propertyNames.errorMessage: Keys starting with _nats are reserved for the server

subject_transform.markdownDescription: Transform the subject of incoming messages before they are stored (server 2.10+).

markdownEnumDescriptions: S2 (Snappy-compatible) compression: smaller files, a little more CPU.
compression.markdownDescription: On-disk compression for file storage (server 2.10+). Can be changed on an existing stream (applies to new blocks).

consumer_limits.markdownDescription: Defaults (and upper bounds) for consumers that don't set these themselves (server 2.10+).

inactive_threshold.markdownDescription:
Default `inactive_threshold` for consumers of this stream.

**Unit: nanoseconds** (JetStream API). `1000000000` = 1 s · `60000000000` = 1 min · `3600000000000` = 1 h · `86400000000000` = 24 h.

max_ack_pending.markdownDescription: Default (and maximum) `max_ack_pending` for consumers of this stream.

first_seq.markdownDescription: First sequence number used by a new stream (e.g. to continue numbering after a migration). Not for mirrors / sources.

subject_delete_marker_ttl.markdownDescription:
When a message is removed by `max_age` (or a purge / delete), leave a delete marker with this TTL so watchers see the removal (server 2.11+). Requires `allow_msg_ttl`.

**Unit: nanoseconds** (JetStream API). `1000000000` = 1 s · `60000000000` = 1 min · `3600000000000` = 1 h · `86400000000000` = 24 h.

allow_msg_ttl.markdownDescription:
Honour the per-message `Nats-TTL` header (server 2.11+).

⚠ **One-way** — can be turned on with an update but never turned off again.

allow_msg_counter.markdownDescription:
Turn the stream into a distributed counter (CRDT increments via the `Nats-Incr` header, server 2.12+).

⛔ **Immutable** — cannot be changed on an existing stream; the plan flags the change and apply is blocked. Recreate the stream instead.

allow_msg_schedules.markdownDescription:
Allow scheduled / delayed messages (`Nats-Schedule` headers, server 2.12+). Cannot be combined with `discard: "new"`.

⚠ **One-way** — can be turned on with an update but never turned off again.

allow_atomic.markdownDescription: Allow atomic batch publishes: all messages of a batch are stored or none (server 2.12+).

allow_batched.markdownDescription: Allow (non-atomic) batched publishing with a single acknowledgement per batch (server 2.14+).

markdownEnumDescriptions: Sync to disk before sending the PubAck. **Default**, strongest durability.
Send the PubAck before the disk sync completes: much higher throughput, small window of loss if a server crashes (mitigated by replicas).
persist_mode.markdownDescription:
Disk sync model (server 2.12+).

⛔ **Immutable** — cannot be changed on an existing stream; the plan flags the change and apply is blocked. Recreate the stream instead.

subjects.errorMessage: A mirror stream cannot have subjects

sources.errorMessage: A mirror stream cannot have sources
